what: Serial double pendulum and physical bracing. This 76-piece control adds six real brace and pin pieces to the 70-piece double pendulum. Both links become one rigid assembly while the upper pivot remains free. Six real brace pieces lock the elbow while the upper pivot remains free. Run the same pulse and observe a moving tip with no relative elbow motion.
try: Choose this example: its Blocks program loads automatically. Reset to the saved pose before each run, then press Run.
The support moves from 0° to 90° slowly at 30°/s, waits 0.3 s, then returns at 180°/s. Watch the quick return excite the free links.
During the 12-second observation, the support stays held while the links can keep moving. Compare upper, lower and relative elbow angles; the motor encoder measures the support.
Reset and choose the companion Cascade example. Both use the same program. Compare the free elbow with the six-piece physical brace.
why: Moving the support excites the passive links. Once the support is held, gravity and inertia govern their two coupled angles. Holding the motor does not hold either free joint. The physical brace removes relative elbow freedom while leaving the top pivot free.
matters: Independent angles distinguish a two-link mechanism from a single rigid pendulum. A moving tip alone does not prove that every joint is moving.
question: Does a moving lower tip prove that the elbow is free?
answer: No. The braced links swing together around the upper pivot while their relative elbow angle stays constant. Compare this with the unbraced model using the same motor route. The added brace changes mass and inertia as well as removing one degree of freedom.
further: The real brace also adds mass and inertia, so this comparison is not a mass-matched measurement of natural frequency.
Completion ends the support route and observation. It does not require the passive links to settle. Reset before repeating the experiment.
Compare independent link angles, not the freely spinning elbow pin. Stay within the saved 0°–90° motor route.
formula: Kinematic definitions: q₁ and q₂ are independently observed link angles about the common hinge axis; the relative elbow angle is Δ=q₂−q₁. In an ideal planar projection, tip−support = 80u(q₁)+48u(q₂) mm, where u(q) is the downward unit vector rotated through q in that plane. The two link lengths sum to 128 mm. This is a geometric relationship, not a time-history or energy prediction. In the saved straight brace control, Δ is constant; the one remaining pendulum angle may still vary.
